messages:
sara: quick flag — ran a quantized bring-up in the eval CI matrix and noticed prompt snippets from customer X in /tmp/eval-cache shared between runners. reproducible locally with parallel jobs. not sure if it's raw prompt text or metadata leakage. can someone triage?

miguel: ugh. can you paste the repro steps?

sara: steps are tiny: 
```
# run two runner workers concurrently
CI_JOB_ID=local1 python runner.py --evalset dialogs.json --quantize 8bit --cache /tmp/eval-cache &
CI_JOB_ID=local2 python runner.py --evalset dialogs.json --quantize 8bit --cache /tmp/eval-cache &
wait
```
then look at /tmp/eval-cache/kv/ for small plaintext fragments — observation: fragments look like truncated prompts.

priya: thanks. that sounds like the KV cache directory isn't namespaced per-job when the quantized runtime falls back to disk. we've seen similar with the on-prem runner when tmpdir wasn't unique.

alex: @sara can you confirm whether these are full prompts or just tokenized ids? if it's plain text that's a PII issue and we need a sec escalation.

sara: they're small segments of the original prompt (user instructions). some have names/IDs. not full customer secrets but still not okay.

miguel: probable cause: the quant runtime's disk spill path uses a shared path and stores serialized cache blobs that still contain de-tokenized text for easier debugging. bad default.

ci-bot: CI warning — job 1876544321 duplicated cache path detected (policy: eval-runner/tmp-isolation).

priya: immediate fixes: 1) patch runner to use per-job mkdtemp under allowed workspace (e.g. /var/tmp/eval-${CI_JOB_ID}) 2) sanitize/strip any human-readable fields from on-disk blobs 3) add unit+integration test to CI matrix that runs two parallel jobs and checks no cross-file overlap.

alex: agree. also add an assertion in the serializer to never write `prompt_text` fields to disk unless explicitly enabled with a flag.

miguel: I'll open a PR for the tmpdir + serializer assertion. will also add a small fuzz test to try concurrent writes.

ops-bot: ops-note — scheduled a short maintenance window for the staging eval cluster at 2026-03-21T02:00Z to run a cache-sweep script.

priya: security ask: can @security confirm whether the current incident requires disclosure? my read: low-risk since only partial snippets, no creds, and only in staging/CI, but we should audit access logs.

alex: pinging @security (cc eng-infra).

sara: quick mitigation pushed to CI config: set EVAL_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d /var/tmp/eval-XXXX) per job and enable `strip_prompt_text=true` flag — tests running now. will report back.

miguel: PR 4723 created: runner: per-job cache dir + serializer hard-sanitizer. includes new integration test `tests/integration/test_cache_isolation.py`. link: https://git.redwood/infra/runner/pulls/4723

ci-bot: PR 4723 — pipeline passed (unit + integration), but flake in lint step.

alex: leaving a comment on the PR to ensure we don't re-enable human-readable dumps by default. also add a changelog entry and a note for Dedicated/Private deploy docs.

priya: follow-ups: - add IAM audit to find who had read access to staging blob store in last 14 days - add a gating e2e in CI that runs parallel quantized jobs weekly - security to run an informal review of serializer schema 

ops-bot: audit job scheduled: iam-audit-staging-2026-03-22.

sara: thanks team. next steps: merge PR after lint fix, rotate any staging keys that touched the cache path, and post a short incident note in #incidents if we confirm any customer data touched persistent storage.

miguel: tl;dr — root cause: shared cache path + human-readable debug fields in on-disk blobs. fix: per-job dirs + strip by default + CI tests.

alex: LGTM. :thumbsup:
